Pha nước chấm với nước mắm, giấm, đường: Mix the fish sauce, vinegar, sugar and warm water; add garlic, chili, papaya and carrot. Balance the sweet-and-sour flavor to taste.
Pha nước mắm chua ngọt riêng và rưới từn: Mix the sweet-sour fish sauce separately and add it gradually so the vermicelli does not become too salty or soggy.

Pha nước mắm, nước và đường, đun sôi rồi: Mix fish sauce, water and sugar, bring to a boil and let cool; Add finely chopped onions.

Phi boa rô, sả với bột cà ri 30 giây; ch: Spicy tilapia, lemongrass with curry powder for 30 seconds; Add soaked beans, vegetarian patties and wood ear fungus and stir for 3 minutes.
Phi boa rô, xào cà chua băm 5–7 phút; th: Stir-fry with sauerkraut and minced tomatoes for 5–7 minutes; Add water and vegetarian seasoning.
Phi boa rô, xào cà rốt, bắp non và nấm 5: Stir-fry with sauerkraut, carrots, baby corn and mushrooms for 5–7 minutes; Add vegetarian seasoning and water.
Phi boa rô, xào nấm 3 phút, thêm vào nướ: Stir-fry the tilapia, stir-fry the mushrooms for 3 minutes, add to the broth with the beans and vegetarian patties; cook 5–8 minutes and season.
Phi boa rô, xào nấm và cà rốt 3–4 phút r: Add the tilapia, stir-fry the mushrooms and carrots for 3–4 minutes and then add to the porridge.
Phi boa rô, xào sơ cà chua, cà rốt hoặc: Stir-fry sautéed tomatoes, carrots or mushrooms for 2–3 minutes.

Phi hành boa-rô với dầu đến thơm, cho cà: Sauté the leek in oil until fragrant, then add the tomatoes and cook until softened. Add the vegetable stock, mushrooms, vegetarian shrimp paste, seasoning powder, sugar and salt; simmer gently for 12 minutes.

Phi hành tím và sả với dầu. Cho tôm khô,: Fry the shallots and lemongrass in oil. Add the dried shrimp, pork for the sauce and fermented rice lees; stir in the water, toasted rice flour, salt, sugar and pepper.

Phi hành tím với ít dầu, cho cá nục và c: Sauté the shallot in a little oil, then add the mackerel and tomato and turn gently. Add fish sauce, sugar, and enough water to cover; simmer until the fish is cooked and the broth lightly concentrated. Strain and keep the broth hot for dipping.
Phi hành tím, cho ba chỉ vào xào săn. Th: Sauté the shallots, then brown the pork belly. Add the eggplant and pineapple, then pour in the bone broth and strained fish-paste base.

Phi hành tỏi 30–45 giây, cho thịt đã thá: Fry onion and garlic for 30–45 seconds, add thinly sliced meat and stir over medium high heat for 4–6 minutes.
Phi hành tỏi với dầu trên lửa vừa, cho t: Fry onion and garlic with oil over medium heat, add marinated meat and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until meat is firm.
Phi hành tỏi với dầu điều, cho bò ướp bộ: Fry onions and garlic with cashew oil, add beef marinated with braised beef powder, lemongrass and spices and stir for 5 minutes.

Phi hành tỏi, cho thịt lọc xương thái mỏ: Saute onion and garlic, add thinly sliced deboned meat and stir-fry over medium high heat for 6-8 minutes.
Phi hành tỏi, cho tôm ráo vào đảo lửa vừ: Fry onion and garlic, add dried shrimp and stir over medium high heat for 2-3 minutes until color changes.
Phi hành tỏi, xào gà săn, thêm nước dừa: Fry onion and garlic, stir-fry chicken, add coconut milk and water; stew over low heat for 25–30 minutes.
Phi hành tỏi, xào phần nội tạng ở lửa vừ: Fry the onion and garlic, stir-fry the internal organs over medium high heat until completely cooked, then remove.

Phi hành với dầu trên lửa vừa, cho thịt: Fry the onions with oil over medium heat, add the marinated meat and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until the meat is firm.
Phi hành với dầu điều, xào gạch và nấm 3: Sauté onions with cashew oil, stir-fry mushrooms and mushrooms for 3 minutes then add to broth; Add cooked shrimp.
Phi hành với dầu, cho cà chua băm vào đả: Fry onions with oil, add minced tomatoes and stir-fry for 5–7 minutes over medium heat.
Phi hành với dầu, rót trứng và nhân thàn: Fry onions with oil, pour eggs and stuffing into a layer that is not too thick; fry over medium low heat for 4–6 minutes.
Phi hành xào cà chua, thêm nước xương và: Stir-fry onions and tomatoes, add bone broth and vinegar; Season and drop fried beans.
Phi hành đến vàng nhạt, dọn xôi với đậu: Fry onions until light golden, serve sticky rice with beans and onions, drizzle with a little onion oil.
Phi hành, cho thịt băm vào tán rời, xào: Fry the onions, add the minced meat and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until firm.
Phi hành, cho thịt băm vào tán tơi 3–4 p: Fry the onions, add minced meat and fry for 3-4 minutes; Add tomatoes, stir for 3 minutes.
Phi hành, cho tép khô đã rửa nhanh vào đ: Fry the onions, add the quickly washed dried shrimp and stir for 1 minute, then add the corn.

Phi hành, gừng, sả và nghệ, cho gà đã ướ: Fry onions, ginger, lemongrass and turmeric, add marinated chicken and stir-fry for 5 minutes.

Phi hành, xào cà chua 4–5 phút, thêm nướ: Fry onions, saute tomatoes for 4–5 minutes, add water and bring to a boil.

Phi hành, xào phần nội tạng ở lửa vừa lớ: Fry the onions, stir-fry the internal organs over medium high heat until completely cooked, then take them out.

Phi tỏi và một nửa gừng thái sợi, cho bò: Fry the garlic and half the sliced ginger, add the marinated beef and stir-fry for 5 minutes.

Phi tỏi, hành và sả, cho gà đã ướp vào x: Fry garlic, onions and lemongrass, add marinated chicken and stir-fry for 5 minutes.

Phi tỏi, sả hoặc nghệ, cho ếch chặt miến: Fry garlic, lemongrass or turmeric, add cut frog pieces and stir-fry for 6-8 minutes until firm.
Phi tỏi, sả nếu có, cho ốc vào xào lửa v: Stir-fry garlic and lemongrass if any, add snails and stir-fry over medium high heat for 4-6 minutes with spices.

Phi tỏi, xào bò thái mỏng 2–3 phút đến g: Stir-fry garlic, stir-fry thinly sliced beef for 2-3 minutes until almost cooked, take out; Remove the frying oil if there is too much.
Phi tỏi, xào bắp non, nấm và rau củ 4–5: Fry garlic, stir-fry baby corn, mushrooms and vegetables for 4-5 minutes, add tomatoes and seasoning.

Phi tỏi, xào cà chua băm 3–4 phút cho mề: Sauté garlic and minced tomatoes for 3–4 minutes until soft.
Phi tỏi, xào cà chua và dứa 2–3 phút, th: Fry the garlic, stir-fry tomatoes and pineapple for 2–3 minutes, add water and filtered tamarind.

Pa pỉnh tộp là cá tươi tẩm rau thơm và m: Pa pinh top is a Thai dish from Son La: fresh fish seasoned with herbs and mak khen, folded and grilled. Bep Viet has adapted a home-cooking version using cleaned carp or stream fish, grilled over charcoal or in an oven.

Bánh cuốn Cao Bằng được ăn nóng với nước: Cao Bang rice rolls are served hot with bone broth instead of the fish-sauce dip found elsewhere. This version uses thin rice sheets, minced pork and wood-ear mushroom filling, and hot broth; egg can be cooked into the roll as it is locally.
Chả ram tôm đất Bình Định gói tôm đất cù: Binh Dinh land-shrimp rolls wrap small sweet shrimp and pork belly in thin rice paper and fry them until golden. Bep Viet keeps the filling simple so the shrimp stands out, serving fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce on the side.

Cho nước cốt dừa dão, đường, muối và một: Add the thin coconut milk, sugar, salt and half the chili. Cover, bring to a boil, reduce to medium heat and cook, stirring a few times, until the snails are fully cooked, about 8–10 minutes after the liquid returns to a boil.
Thêm nước cốt dừa đặc và phần lớn rau ră: Add the thick coconut milk and most of the Vietnamese coriander. Simmer for another 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens around the shells. Taste, finish with the remaining chili and coriander, and serve hot.
Phá lấu bò là món ăn đường phố quen thuộ: Beef pha lau is a familiar street food in Ho Chi Minh City. Sources describe beef offal cleaned carefully, seasoned with five-spice and aromatics, then simmered in coconut water. Bếp Việt has adapted a home-size batch with commonly available beef tripe, cooked until tender and served with baguette, Vietnamese coriander and a sweet-sour dipping sauce.
Bốn tô nhỏ phá lấu, ăn kèm bánh mì và ra: Four small bowls of pha lau, served with baguette and Vietnamese coriander.
Miếng lòng bò mềm nhưng còn độ giòn, thấ: Tender but slightly springy offal absorbs five-spice and coconut; the amber broth smells of ginger, star anise and cinnamon.
Cắt lòng thành miếng vừa ăn, chan nước d: Cut the offal into bite-size pieces and ladle over hot broth. Serve with crisp baguette, Vietnamese coriander and a lime dipping sauce.
Phá lấu bò Sài Gòn với lòng bò mềm trong: Saigon beef pha lau with tender offal in an amber coconut and five-spice broth, baguette and Vietnamese coriander, isolated on a transparent background.

Chần lòng ngắn rồi rửa lại giúp giảm mùi: Brief blanching and rinsing reduce strong aromas without over-tightening the offal before braising.

Chần lòng trong nồi nước sôi có vài lát: Blanch the offal in boiling water with a few ginger slices and shallot for about 3 minutes. Lift it out, rinse again, scrape away any remaining residue and cut into large pieces.
Rang hoa hồi và quế đến khi thơm. Ướp lò: Lightly toast the star anise and cinnamon. Marinate the offal for 30 minutes with fish sauce, palm sugar, five-spice, curry powder, annatto oil, garlic and shallot.
Phi thơm phần hành tỏi còn lại trong nồi: Heat the remaining shallot and garlic in a pot until fragrant. Add the marinated offal and stir until the surfaces are firm and aromatic.

Thêm nước cốt dừa đặc, nấu thêm 5 phút ở: Add the thick coconut milk and simmer gently for another 5 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and fish sauce; if the broth is too thick, add a little hot water.
Pha nước chấm bằng nước cốt tắc, chút nư: Mix calamansi juice with a little fish sauce and sugar for a dipping sauce. Cut the offal into bite-size pieces, ladle over broth, add Vietnamese coriander and serve hot with baguette.
Tư liệu di sản Hội An ghi nhận chè kê tr: Hoi An heritage records include millet sweet porridge among the offerings for the Doan Ngo festival. A recipe presented with guidance from a culinary artisan combines millet and mung beans and serves the porridge with toasted rice crackers for scooping. Bếp Việt has edited a plant-based batch without dairy or animal fat, cooked until thick enough to eat by spoon or with rice crackers.

Hạt kê nở mềm, quyện cùng đậu xanh nghiề: Soft millet grains blend with mashed mung beans into a thick golden porridge with gentle sweetness; crisp sesame crackers add contrast.

Ngâm kê và đậu xanh riêng để hai nguyên: Soak millet and mung beans separately so both soften evenly.

Cho đậu xanh đã nghiền vào nồi kê, thêm: Stir the mashed mung beans into the millet. Add the sugar and salt and cook gently for another 5–8 minutes until the porridge comes together and thickens.
Tắt bếp, khuấy vani nếu dùng. Múc chè ra: Turn off the heat and stir in the vanilla, if using. Spoon into bowls and serve warm or cooled with toasted sesame rice crackers.
Bánh xèo bông điên điển: Mekong Delta Sesbania Flower Bánh Xèo
Bánh xèo bông điên điển gắn với mùa nước: Sesbania flower bánh xèo is associated with the Mekong Delta flood season, when the yellow blossoms are placed in the filling rather than served only as a side green. Bếp Việt edits a home batch with shrimp, pork belly, bean sprouts and seasonal sesbania flowers; a light coconut mixture makes the crepe fragrant while keeping it crisp. Use only flowers sold as food from a safe source, wash them well and drain thoroughly.

Ăn ngay khi bánh còn nóng. Bẻ miếng bánh: Serve hot. Break off a piece, wrap it with lettuce and herbs, then dip it in tamarind fish sauce. Do not stack the crepes for long, as trapped steam softens the crust.

Cơm lam là cách nấu nếp trong ống tre ho: Cơm lam is a way of cooking glutinous rice in bamboo or reed tubes over a fire and is recorded across several Northwest provinces. Bếp Việt edits a home batch with overnight-soaked upland sticky rice, a little salt and ginger; the rice cooks tender and fragrant inside the young bamboo membrane. Families and local areas differ in seasoning, tube choice and accompaniments.
Bốn ống tre nhỏ, mỗi người một ống; dùng: Four small bamboo tubes, one per person; serve with sesame salt or grilled dishes.
Nếp chín dẻo đều trong ống tre, hạt bóng: Evenly cooked sticky rice in bamboo tubes, glossy and tender with a light roasted-bamboo aroma; serve with nutty sesame salt.
Để ống cơm nguội bớt rồi bóc lớp tre già: Let the tubes cool slightly, peel away the outer bamboo and keep the thin inner membrane attached to the rice. Cut into serving pieces and eat with sesame salt; grilled stream fish or pork can be served alongside.
Bốn ống cơm lam nếp nương nướng vàng trê: Four roasted Northwest sticky-rice bamboo tubes on a ceramic platter, one split to show glossy rice with a bowl of sesame salt; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 9 giờ 10 phút, gồm thời gian ngâm: About 9 hours 10 minutes, including overnight rice soaking; grilling time varies with tube size and coal heat.

Ngâm nếp đủ thời gian rồi để ráo để cơm: Soak and drain the rice well so it cooks evenly without a hard center.

Nút miệng ống bằng lá chuối sạch hoặc mộ: Plug the openings with clean banana leaf or young bamboo leaf. Prepare a steady bed of glowing coals without large flames.
Đặt các ống lên vỉ cách than vừa phải. X: Set the tubes on a rack above the coals. Turn each tube regularly so the bamboo heats evenly and does not burn on one side.
Grill for about 40–50 minutes, depending on tube thickness. The rice is ready when it smells cooked, the bamboo contracts and a test grain is tender throughout.

Bánh canh ghẹ là món nước biển quen thuộ: Bánh canh ghẹ is a familiar seafood noodle soup in Vũng Tàu; its broth is commonly simmered with crab and pork bones for a rounded natural sweetness. Bếp Việt edits a home version with thick bánh canh noodles, blue swimmer crab, shallot and a little annatto oil for a warm, clear broth.
Bốn tô vừa, mỗi tô có một phần ghẹ và sợ: Four medium bowls, each with one portion of crab and thick noodles.
Tô bánh canh nóng có sợi dày mềm dai, th: A hot bowl of thick, pleasantly chewy noodles with sweet crab meat and a clean, seafood-forward broth topped with a little scallion and cilantro.
Xếp bánh canh vào tô, chan nước dùng sôi: Place the noodles in bowls and ladle over boiling broth. Add the crab meat, claws, scallion and cilantro. Serve hot with pepper, lime and chili to taste.
Tô bánh canh ghẹ Vũng Tàu có sợi bánh ca: A bowl of Vũng Tàu bánh canh with thick noodles, crab meat and claws in a light golden broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 15 phút, gồm sơ chế, hầm nư: About 1 hour 15 minutes for prep, broth and crab; fresh noodles shorten the cooking time.
Chọn ghẹ còn tươi, vỏ nguyên; hấp ghẹ ri: Choose fresh crabs with intact shells; steaming them separately keeps the meat from breaking down in the broth.
Hớt bọt khi hầm xương để nước dùng trong: Skim the pork-bone broth as it simmers for a clearer, cleaner flavor.
Chần bánh canh riêng nếu sợi có nhiều bộ: Blanch the noodles separately if they have excess surface starch, so the soup does not become too thick.

Blanch briefly and rinse before simmering.

Peel and crush; some will be fried until fragrant.
Nêm cuối, điều chỉnh theo độ mặn của nướ: Season near the end, adjusting to the broth's saltiness.
Chần xương ống trong nước sôi 3 phút, rử: Blanch the pork bones in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse. Scrub the crabs clean, remove the apron and gills, and drain.
Hành tím bóc vỏ, đập dập; hành lá và ngò: Peel and crush the shallots. Wash and chop the scallions and cilantro. If the noodles have a heavy coating of starch, rinse briefly and drain.
Cho xương vào nồi với 1,8 lít nước. Đun: Simmer the bones in 1.8 liters of water. Bring to a boil, skim, then cook gently for 35 minutes; strain the broth if needed.
Hấp ghẹ 8–10 phút đến khi vỏ chuyển đỏ c: Steam the crabs for 8–10 minutes, until the shells turn red-orange and the meat is just cooked. Cool slightly, pick the meat and keep a few claws whole for serving.
Phi hành tím với dầu điều, cho thịt ghẹ: Fry the shallots in annatto oil, add the crab meat and gently stir for 1 minute. Add it to the broth and season with fish sauce, salt and rock sugar.
Chần bánh canh theo hướng dẫn trên bao b: Blanch the noodles following the package directions and divide among four bowls. Pour over the boiling broth, add crab meat and claws, scallion, cilantro and pepper.
Bò một nắng muối kiến vàng Krông Pa: Krông Pa One-Sun Beef with Ant-Egg Salt
Bò một nắng chấm muối kiến vàng là cặp m: One-sun beef served with muối kiến vàng is a regional pairing associated with Krông Pa, Gia Lai and Central Highlands food culture. The beef is seasoned and dried in the sun for a day before it is cooked for serving; this Bếp Việt home version uses commercially prepared, labeled one-sun beef, quickly grilled and served with food-grade ant-egg salt.
Một đĩa 500 g bò đã chế biến, chia ăn cù: One 500 g plate of prepared beef to share with vegetables and rice paper for 3–4 people.
Thịt bò một nắng nóng thơm, mặt ngoài xé: Warm one-sun beef with lightly charred edges and tender slices inside; muối kiến vàng adds savory, tangy, spicy and aromatic notes.
Rest the beef for 3 minutes, then slice across the grain. Serve with muối kiến vàng, herbs or rice paper, following the package's storage and cooking instructions.
Thịt bò một nắng Gia Lai đã nướng và thá: Grilled and sliced Gia Lai one-sun beef on a ceramic plate with a bowl of muối kiến vàng and a lime wedge; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 22 phút khi dùng bò một nắng đã c: About 22 minutes using prepared one-sun beef; the traditional seasoning and sun-drying time is not part of this reheating recipe.
Chọn sản phẩm bò một nắng có nhãn, hạn d: Choose labeled one-sun beef with a clear use-by date and storage directions; thaw in the refrigerator if frozen.
Làm nóng vỉ trước, nướng nhanh từng mặt: Preheat the grill and cook briefly on each side; prolonged grilling makes the meat dry and tough.
Muối kiến vàng có thể chứa dị nguyên từ: Muối kiến vàng may contain insect allergens; check ingredients and avoid it if you have a related allergy.
Mua sản phẩm có nhãn và bảo quản đúng hư: Choose a labeled product and store it as directed; thaw in the refrigerator if needed.
Dùng sản phẩm đóng gói có nguồn gốc rõ r: Use a packaged product with a clear source; check for allergens.
Cut into wedges and serve to taste.
Kiểm tra nhãn, hạn sử dụng và tình trạng: Check the label, use-by date and storage condition of the one-sun beef and ant-egg salt. If frozen, thaw in the refrigerator and pat the surface dry.
Rửa rau thơm, để ráo; cắt chanh thành mi: Wash and drain the herbs; cut the lime into wedges. Preheat a grill or cast-iron pan over medium heat.
Quét rất mỏng dầu lên vỉ nếu cần. Nướng: Lightly oil the grill if needed. Grill the beef for about 2–3 minutes per side, turning once, until heated through and lightly charred; follow the producer's directions.
Gắp thịt ra, để nghỉ 3 phút rồi thái nga: Remove the beef, rest for 3 minutes and slice thinly across the grain. Arrange with muối kiến vàng, herbs, lime and rice paper.
Cháo canh cá lóc Quảng Bình: Quảng Bình Cháo Canh with Snakehead Fish
Cháo canh là món đặc sản dân dã của Quản: Cháo canh is a rustic specialty of Quảng Bình. Despite the word cháo, the dish is a noodle soup made with thick wheat- or rice-flour noodles, snakehead fish, meat and mustard greens. Bếp Việt edits a fish version with pork-bone stock, củ nén and turmeric; fresh noodles are used to simplify the home preparation.
Bốn tô vừa, mỗi tô có sợi bột dày, cá ló: Four medium bowls, each with thick dough noodles, snakehead fish and mustard greens.
Sợi bột dày mềm dai nằm trong nước dùng: Thick, tender noodles in a hot broth with lightly turmeric-colored snakehead fish and just-cooked mustard greens; the broth is gently thickened, not like rice porridge.
Múc khi còn sôi nóng, rắc hành lá và tiê: Serve while piping hot with scallion and black pepper. Crispy ram rolls can accompany the bowl as they do in local servings; add chili if desired.

Khoảng 1 giờ 5 phút với sợi tươi bán sẵn: About 1 hour 5 minutes with fresh noodles; cooking time varies with the noodle type.
Chọn sợi cháo canh tươi hoặc đóng gói, đ: Choose fresh or packaged cháo canh noodles and follow the package cooking time so they do not break down.
Luộc cá vừa chín rồi gỡ xương kỹ; lọc nư: Cook the fish just until done, remove all bones carefully and strain the poaching liquid for a clean broth.
Cho rau cải vào sau cùng, nước sôi lại l: Add the mustard greens at the end; once the broth returns to a boil, turn off the heat to keep the greens bright and crisp.

Chần xương heo 3 phút trong nước sôi, rử: Blanch the pork bones for 3 minutes in boiling water and rinse. Clean and cut the fish; season it with half the fish sauce, turmeric and a little salt for 10 minutes.
Rau cải rửa sạch, thái khúc. Củ nén bóc: Wash and cut the mustard greens. Peel and crush the củ nén; wash and slice the scallions. Prepare the noodles according to the package directions.
Hầm xương với 1,5 lít nước trong 30 phút: Simmer the bones in 1.5 liters of water for 30 minutes, skimming regularly. Poach the fish separately until just cooked, lift it out to remove the bones and strain the poaching liquid into the stock.
Phi thơm củ nén với dầu ăn. Cho cá đã gỡ: Fry the củ nén in oil until fragrant. Add the picked fish and gently turn for 1–2 minutes with the remaining fish sauce, keeping the pieces intact.
Nêm nước dùng với muối, tiêu và nước mắm: Season the broth with salt, pepper and fish sauce. Add the cháo canh noodles and cook according to the package timing until tender and slightly chewy, and the broth is lightly thickened.
Cho cá và rau cải vào nồi, đun sôi lại k: Return the fish to the pot, add the mustard greens and bring back to a boil for about 1 minute. Turn off the heat, ladle into bowls and top with scallions and pepper.
Bánh tẻ Phú Nhi là thức quà xứ Đoài làm: Phu Nhi rice cakes are a Xu Doai specialty made from wet-ground rice batter and filled with pork, wood-ear mushrooms and shallots before being wrapped in leaves and boiled. Bếp Việt adapts the traditional technique for a small home batch, stirring the batter until smooth and pliable without letting it become pasty.
Khoảng 8 bánh thon dài, mỗi người 2 bánh: About eight slender cakes, two per person, served warm with a light dipping sauce.
Bánh nóng có dáng thon gọn, lớp bột gạo: Each warm cake has a neat slender shape, a tender ivory rice casing and a savory pork filling with lightly crisp mushrooms and fragrant shallots.
Bóc lá khi bánh còn ấm, ăn cùng dưa góp: Unwrap while warm and enjoy with pickled vegetables or a little dipping sauce. Re-steam briefly if the cakes cool; avoid boiling them again, which can make the casing waterlogged.
Bánh tẻ Phú Nhi gói lá xanh, một chiếc m: Phu Nhi rice cakes wrapped in green leaves, with one opened to show a tender rice casing and pork and wood-ear mushroom filling; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

bánh gạo nhân thịt gói lá: Vietnamese pork rice cakes in leaves
Ngâm gạo đủ mềm rồi xay với nước; lọc bộ: Soak the rice until soft, then blend it thoroughly; strain if any coarse grains remain.
Quấy bột trên lửa nhỏ liên tục, dừng khi: Stir the batter over low heat until just thickened and still pliable. Overcooked batter is difficult to spread around the filling.

Rehydrate the wood-ear mushrooms, rinse and mince. Mince the pork and shallots, then season with fish sauce and pepper.
Phi thơm hành với dầu, cho thịt vào xào: Sauté the shallots in oil, add the pork and cook until crumbly. Add the mushrooms, stir until the filling is fairly dry, then season to taste.
Rửa lá, chần nhanh qua nước nóng cho mềm: Wash and briefly blanch the leaves to make them pliable. Wipe them dry and prepare ties and a pot of water.
Đổ bột gạo đã xay vào nồi đáy dày, đun l: Pour the rice batter into a heavy saucepan. Stir constantly over low heat; when it begins to thicken, remove from the heat and keep stirring until smooth and pliable but still spreadable.
Trải lá, phết lớp bột mỏng theo chiều dà: Spread a thin layer of batter lengthwise on a leaf, add a line of filling and cover with a little more batter. Fold into a slender parcel, tuck in both ends and tie gently.
Xếp bánh vào nồi nước sôi nhẹ, luộc 35–4: Place the parcels in gently boiling water and cook for 35–40 minutes, depending on their size. Turn them once; the casing should look slightly translucent with no raw batter at the center.
Vớt bánh, để ráo và nghỉ 5 phút trước kh: Lift out, drain and rest for five minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers and re-steam the same day before eating.
Bánh ram ít Huế ghép hai kết cấu trong m: Hue bánh ram ít combines two textures in one bite: a soft glutinous-rice dumpling filled with shrimp and pork, set on a crisp fried rice base. Bếp Việt edits a home-sized batch with lightly seasoned filling and a sweet-sour fish sauce for serving.
Khoảng 12 chiếc bánh nhỏ, mỗi người 3 ch: About twelve small dumplings, three per person, served while the crispy bases are fresh.
Đế bánh mỏng giòn nâng viên bánh ít trắn: A golden crisp base supports a tender ivory dumpling with savory shrimp and pork, a little scallion oil and a gentle chili-lime dip.
Xếp bánh ít lên đế ram ngay trước khi dọ: Assemble each dumpling on its crispy base just before serving. Eat warm with lightly sweetened garlic-chili fish sauce to balance the richness and chewiness.
Bánh ram ít Huế xếp trên đĩa, viên bánh: Hue bánh ram ít on a plate, each shrimp and pork sticky-rice dumpling resting on a crisp golden base; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

Châm nước ấm vào bột từng ít một, dừng k: Add warm water to the glutinous-rice flour gradually until the dough is smooth and not sticky.
Đế ram cần hấp chín rồi để nguội, thấm k: Steam the bases first, let them cool and pat dry before frying to make them crisp with less splatter.

Trộn bột nếp với muối, rót nước ấm từng: Mix the glutinous-rice flour with salt. Gradually add warm water and knead until smooth and non-sticky. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Băm tôm và thịt ba chỉ. Ướp với một phần: Mince the shrimp and pork belly. Season with some fish sauce, sugar, pepper and shallots; leave for ten minutes.
Pha phần nước mắm còn lại với đường, nướ: Mix the remaining fish sauce and sugar with warm water, lime juice, garlic and chili. Stir to dissolve and taste.

Bếp Việt edits a home version with pumpkin, sweet potato, taro, green banana, long beans, mushrooms, tofu skin and peanuts; the ingredients are added in stages so tender vegetables keep their shape.

Nồi canh có nước dừa vàng nhạt, ngọt tự: A pale-golden coconut broth carries the natural sweetness of pumpkin and root vegetables. Each piece of vegetable, mushroom and tofu skin stays distinct, creating a gently rich plant-based soup.
Dọn nóng với cơm trắng hoặc bún. Múc nhẹ: Serve hot with rice or vermicelli. Ladle gently so the vegetables stay intact; if using thick coconut cream, dilute it to keep the broth from becoming heavy.

món chay nấu bí khoai: Vietnamese vegetarian pumpkin and taro soup

Nếu muốn khoai môn giữ dáng, áp chảo sơ: If desired, lightly pan-sear the taro in a little oil until the outside is just set.
Đun nước lọc với khoảng một nửa nước cốt: Bring the water and half the coconut milk to a simmer. Add sweet potato, taro and green banana; cook over medium heat for 12–15 minutes until nearly tender.

Rót phần nước cốt dừa còn lại, nêm muối: Pour in the remaining coconut milk, season with salt and a little sugar, then simmer for 3–4 minutes. Taste and turn off the heat once the pumpkin is just tender.
Rắc đậu phộng rang trước khi dọn. Dùng n: Scatter roasted peanuts over the soup. Serve hot with rice or vermicelli; refrigerate leftovers and bring them to a full boil before serving again.
Bún chay Huế có nước dùng thơm nấm và sả: Hue vegetarian bún is a fragrant noodle soup built around mushrooms and lemongrass, served with rice vermicelli, fried tofu, wheat gluten, bamboo shoots and greens. Bếp Việt edits a fully plant-based home version with a vegetable-and-mushroom broth; check packaged seasonings to avoid animal-derived ingredients.

Tô bún nóng có nước dùng trong thơm mùi: A hot bowl with clear lemongrass-scented broth, gentle mushroom sweetness, golden tofu, tender chewy wheat gluten and green vegetables makes a light but satisfying meal.
Chần bún riêng, xếp vào tô rồi chan nước: Blanch the noodles separately, place them in bowls, then ladle over the simmering broth with mushrooms, bamboo shoots, tofu and wheat gluten. Add herbs, pepper or chili and serve at once so the noodles stay springy.
Tô bún chay Huế có bún trắng, đậu hũ chi: A bowl of Hue vegetarian bún with white rice vermicelli, fried tofu, wheat gluten, mushrooms, bamboo shoots and herbs in lemongrass broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

Xào nấm và mì căn trước khi cho vào nồi: Sauté the mushrooms and wheat gluten before adding them to deepen the flavor of both the toppings and broth.

Chần bún nhanh, chia sẵn vào bốn tô. Nếu: Blanch the noodles briefly and divide among four bowls. Strain the mushroom soaking liquid through a fine sieve if using.

Cho cải thảo vào nấu đến vừa mềm. Nêm mu: Add napa cabbage and cook just until tender. Season with salt, a little sugar, soy sauce and optional annatto oil; taste for a fragrant, gently savory broth.
Gắp sả ra, chan nước dùng cùng nấm, măng: Remove the lemongrass stalks. Ladle the broth and toppings over the noodles, add herbs and pepper, and serve hot.
Bánh gai Tứ Trụ của làng Mía, Thọ Xuân n: Tu Tru bánh gai from Mia village in Tho Xuan is known for a dark glutinous-rice casing made with ramie leaves, a mung-bean and coconut filling, gentle molasses sweetness and sesame. Bếp Việt adapts a small batch with softened dried ramie leaves and ordinary home equipment; the parcels are wrapped in banana leaf, steamed and cooled so the casing becomes pleasantly chewy.
Khoảng 8 bánh nhỏ, mỗi người 2 bánh; dùn: About eight small cakes, two per person, served cooled with hot tea.
Chiếc bánh vuông nhỏ có vỏ nếp đen bóng,: Each small square cake has a glossy dark casing with the fragrance of ramie leaves, a sweet mung-bean and coconut center, a hint of molasses and a lightly nutty sesame finish.
Để bánh nguội hoàn toàn rồi bóc lớp lá t: Let the cakes cool completely before peeling the inner leaf, since the casing is sticky. Serve in small pieces with hot tea; briefly steam again if a refrigerated cake becomes firm.
Bánh gai Tứ Trụ vỏ đen từ lá gai phủ mè,: Tu Tru bánh gai with a dark ramie-leaf casing, sesame and a mung-bean coconut center, wrapped in banana leaf; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

Sên nhân đến khi ráo vừa đủ vo viên, khô: Cook the filling until it just holds together when rolled; drying it too much makes the center crumbly.

Lau sạch, hơ mềm để gói; lót thêm lá chu: Wipe clean and warm briefly to soften; line with fresh leaves if brittle.

Tán đậu xanh khi còn nóng. Sên với đường: Mash the warm mung beans. Cook with sugar over low heat, add the grated coconut and stir until the filling comes together. Cool and divide into eight balls.

Bún bò cay Bạc Liêu: Bac Lieu spicy beef rice noodles
Bún bò cay Bạc Liêu nổi bật với nước dùn: Bac Lieu spicy beef bún is known for its deep golden broth, the fragrant heat of satay and tender beef served with white rice vermicelli. Bếp Việt adapts a home batch with a lighter broth, keeping Thai basil, lime and chili salt as characteristic accompaniments.
Bốn tô bún vừa, mỗi tô có nước dùng cay,: Four medium bowls with spicy broth, beef and Thai basil; adjust the satay to taste.
Tô bún nóng có nước dùng màu vàng cam tự: A hot bowl of naturally golden-orange broth, tender but distinct beef slices, white vermicelli and fragrant Thai basil; add satay and chili separately to control the heat.
Chần bún, xếp thịt bò rồi chan nước dùng: Briefly blanch the noodles, arrange the beef and ladle over simmering broth. Serve with Thai basil, lime and chili salt; let each person add satay at the table.
Tô bún bò cay Bạc Liêu trong bát sứ trắn: Bac Lieu spicy beef bún in a white ceramic bowl with rice vermicelli, beef, golden-red broth, Thai basil and lime; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 2 giờ 15 phút, phần lớn là thời g: About 2 hours 15 minutes, mostly for simmering the bones and tenderizing the beef.

Bánh chưng đen là biến thể Tày của Lạng: Lang Son black bánh chưng is a Tay variation: glutinous rice is soaked in carefully filtered plant-ash water, then wrapped with mung beans and pork in dong leaves. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch; use only ash water confirmed safe for food and never burn unknown plants to make it.

Bánh vuông có lớp nếp đen bóng, dẻo thơm: A square cake with glossy dark glutinous rice, a nutty yellow mung-bean layer and tender pork; the color comes from the rice treatment, not charring.
Để bánh nghỉ sau khi vớt, ép nhẹ cho ráo: Let the cake rest after boiling, press it lightly to drain, then slice with a clean knife. Serve with pickled onions or vegetables; refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat thoroughly.

Bánh canh Trảng Bàng là món nước Tây Nin: Trảng Bàng bánh canh is a Tay Ninh noodle soup made with thick rice-flour noodles, a clear pork broth, boiled pork and wild greens on the side. Bếp Việt adapts a home version with ready-made fresh noodles; choose seasonal greens such as herbs, perilla, fish mint and mildly sour leaves.

Cháo lươn Vinh là món đặc sản xứ Nghệ, k: Vinh eel porridge is a specialty of Nghe An, pairing slowly cooked rice porridge with field eel sautéed in turmeric, local shallots and chili. Bếp Việt adapts a home method that keeps the eel pieces intact, uses carefully strained eel-bone stock and lets each diner adjust the heat.
Bốn bát cháo sánh với lươn xào riêng, ra: Four bowls of thick porridge topped with separately sautéed eel, herbs and chili to taste; serve with bánh mướt or bread if desired.

Cho lươn vào nồi cùng gừng, một ít muối: Poach the eel with ginger, a little salt and enough water to cover until fully cooked. Transfer it to a clean plate, remove the flesh along the backbone and keep the backbone.
Giã hoặc băm nhỏ xương sống lươn, cho và: Crush or finely chop the backbone, return it to the poaching liquid and simmer for 15 minutes. Strain carefully through a fine sieve and discard all bone fragments.

Phi hành tăm và hành tím với dầu. Cho ng: Fry the local shallots and shallots in oil. Add the turmeric and chili, stir until fragrant, then add eel, fish sauce and a little salt. Sauté briefly until the eel is hot and seasoned.
Nếm lại cháo, múc vào bát rồi đặt lươn x: Taste the porridge, ladle into bowls and top with the sautéed eel. Add rau răm, rice-paddy herb, scallions and pepper; serve hot with bánh mướt or bread.
Bánh căn Nha Trang: Nha Trang rice cakes with shrimp and quail eggs
Bánh căn Nha Trang được đổ thành từng ch: Nha Trang bánh căn are small rice-flour cakes cooked individually in clay molds, with shrimp or quail eggs on top. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch using a multi-well pan and scallion-fish sauce, served with herbs and green mango to balance the savory topping.

Khi viền bánh vừa vàng và đáy tự róc khu: Remove the cake when its edge turns golden and releases from the mold. Repeat in batches, adjusting the heat so the center cooks without darkening the base.
Phi hành lá với phần dầu còn lại, rưới m: Warm the scallions in the remaining oil, spoon a little over the cakes and serve hot with herbs, green mango and dipping sauce.
Cá nục hấp cuốn bánh tráng Đà Nẵng: Da Nang steamed scad with rice-paper rolls
Cá nục hấp cuốn bánh tráng là món dân dã: Steamed scad wrapped in rice paper is a simple coastal Da Nang meal. The fish is steamed with lemongrass, scallion and chili to keep its natural sweetness, then rolled with herbs, noodles and vegetables. Bếp Việt adapts a family-sized portion and includes a safe doneness check.
Bốn phần cá hấp ăn cuốn, có bánh tráng,: Four servings of steamed fish with rice paper, fresh vermicelli, greens and dipping sauce.
Cá nục hấp mềm ngọt, thơm sả hành; cuốn: Tender steamed scad scented with lemongrass and scallions, wrapped in rice paper with fresh herbs, young water spinach and vermicelli; served with fish sauce or fermented anchovy dipping sauce.
Gỡ cá thành miếng, kiểm tra và bỏ hết xư: Flake the fish into pieces and check carefully for pin bones. Wrap with rice paper, noodles and greens; dip in the sweet-sour fish sauce or prepared fermented anchovy sauce.
Cá nục hấp sả hành trên đĩa, ăn cuốn cùn: Steamed scad with lemongrass and scallions, served with rice paper, vermicelli, fresh greens and dipping sauce; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 45 phút; cá hấp nhanh, phần lớn t: About 45 minutes; steaming is quick, while most preparation time goes to the greens and dipping sauce.
Chọn cá tươi, mắt trong và thân chắc; để: Choose fresh fish with clear eyes and firm flesh; keep the raw-fish knife and board separate from the greens.
Hấp vừa chín tới để thịt cá còn mọng. Vớ: Steam just until done so the flesh stays moist. For thicker fish, extend the cooking time and check that the flesh next to the bone is opaque.

Choose 3–4 small fish and clean the gills and innards.
