Rau sống và rau muống non: Fresh greens and young water spinach
Rửa kỹ, để ráo; chẻ rau muống non nếu cọ: Wash well and drain; split thick water-spinach stems.
Adjust to the saltiness of the fish sauce.
Cạo vảy, bỏ mang và ruột cá, rửa nhanh r: Scale and clean the fish, rinse briefly and pat dry. Score shallow cuts on both sides for even cooking.
Đập dập sả, thái gừng và cắt hành lá. Rử: Bruise the lemongrass, slice the ginger and cut the scallions. Wash and drain the greens and young water spinach; blanch the vermicelli if needed.
Hòa nước mắm với đường và nước ấm, thêm: Dissolve sugar in warm water and fish sauce, then add lime, garlic and chili. Taste for a gentle sweet-sour-salty balance.
Lót sả dưới xửng, xếp cá lên trên rồi ph: Line a steamer with lemongrass and arrange the fish on top. Add ginger, scallion and chili; bring the water in the steamer to a boil.
Steam for about 12–18 minutes depending on fish size. The flesh should be opaque and separate easily from the bone; if using a thermometer, the thickest part should reach at least 63°C.
Nhấc cá ra đĩa sạch, giữ lại nước hấp. L: Transfer the fish to a clean platter and reserve the steaming liquid. Strain it and bring it to a boil before adding a little to the dipping sauce, if desired.
Serve the hot fish with rice paper, vermicelli and greens. Flake a small portion at a time, check for bones and eat immediately.
Cháo canh Quảng Bình không phải cháo gạo: Quang Binh chao canh is not smooth rice porridge: it is a hearty soup with thick, pleasantly chewy handmade noodles and a flavorful seafood broth. Bếp Việt adapts a home pot with shrimp and fish, keeping the noodles as the defining feature and seasoning lightly to let the seafood broth shine.
Bốn tô cháo canh sợi dày với tôm, cá và: Four hot bowls of thick noodles with shrimp, fish and broth.
Tô nước dùng nóng có sợi bột to, mềm dai: A hot bowl of thick, tender-chewy noodles with just-cooked shrimp and fish, scallions and pepper in a clear, savory seafood broth.
Múc sợi và nhân vào tô, chan nước dùng đ: Divide the noodles and seafood among bowls and ladle over the hot broth. Finish with scallions, coriander and pepper; serve chili separately.
Tô cháo canh Quảng Bình với sợi bột dày,: A bowl of Quang Binh chao canh with thick noodles, shrimp, fish, scallions and hot broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 35 phút, gồm thời gian nghỉ: About 1 hour 35 minutes including dough resting; fresh store-bought noodles shorten the preparation.
Nếu tự cán sợi, áo bột vừa đủ để sợi khô: If rolling the noodles at home, dust them lightly so they do not stick; shake off excess dry flour before adding them to the pot.
Nấu sợi trong nước dùng sôi nhẹ, khuấy đ: Cook the noodles in a gentle boil and stir the bottom of the pot at the start so they stay separate.
Cho cá vào cuối và giữ lửa vừa để thịt c: Add the fish near the end and maintain a moderate simmer so it cooks through without breaking apart.
Combine with the wheat flour for tender-chewy noodles.
Rót từ từ; lượng thực tế tùy độ hút nước: Pour in gradually; actual absorption varies by flour.
Chia một phần cho bột, phần còn lại nêm: Divide between the dough and the broth.
Bóc vỏ, giữ lại đầu và vỏ để nấu nước ng: Peel and reserve heads and shells for the broth if desired.
Choose fish with firm flesh and remove all bones.
Dùng nấu nước dùng; có thể thay một phần: For the broth; some can be replaced with strained shrimp stock.
Nêm nước dùng sau khi đã có vị ngọt từ h: Season after the seafood has flavored the broth.
Serve on the side to adjust the heat.
Trộn bột mì, bột gạo và muối. Rót nước ấ: Combine wheat flour, rice flour and salt. Gradually add warm water and knead until smooth, elastic and no longer sticky; cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Bóc vỏ tôm, giữ riêng đầu và vỏ nếu dùng: Peel the shrimp and reserve the heads and shells if using them for stock. Rinse the fish, remove all bones and cut it into bite-sized pieces.
Rắc một lớp bột áo mỏng, cán bột dày kho: Dust the work surface lightly, roll the dough 2–3 mm thick and cut it into moderately wide strands. Shake gently to separate them.
Băm hành tím; rửa và thái nhỏ hành lá, r: Mince the shallots; wash and finely slice scallions and coriander. Prepare the seasonings before cooking the noodles.
Phi thơm hành tím với dầu. Nếu dùng đầu: Sauté the shallots in oil. If using shrimp heads, add them and stir until red, add water and simmer for 20 minutes; strain out the solids.
Đun nước dùng sôi nhẹ, nêm muối và nước: Bring the broth to a gentle boil and season with salt and fish sauce. Add the noodles gradually, stirring the bottom gently during the first minute so they do not stick.
Khi sợi bắt đầu nổi và nước hơi sánh, ch: When the noodles begin to float and the broth thickens slightly, add the shrimp until pink, then add the fish and cook just through.
Nếm lại nước dùng, tắt bếp khi cá vừa ch: Taste the broth and turn off the heat once the fish is done. Ladle into bowls and finish with scallions, coriander and pepper; serve chili separately.
Bánh xèo tôm nhảy Quy Nhơn: Quy Nhon sizzling pancakes with fresh shrimp
Bánh xèo tôm nhảy Quy Nhơn thường đổ thà: Quy Nhon bánh xèo tôm nhảy are usually small, crisp-edged pancakes filled with fresh local earth shrimp and eaten with greens. Bếp Việt keeps the cakes small, the batter thin and the shrimp visible, distinguishing this style from larger, richer coconut-milk versions found elsewhere.
Khoảng 12 bánh nhỏ, mỗi người 3 chiếc; d: About 12 small pancakes, three per person, served with greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
Bánh vàng nghệ, nhỏ và giòn ở mép, giữa: Small golden turmeric pancakes with crisp edges, earth shrimp and bean sprouts, wrapped in fresh greens and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce.
Dọn bánh khi còn nóng cùng xà lách, rau: Serve the pancakes hot with lettuce, herbs and fish sauce. Break off a bite-sized piece, wrap it in greens and dip lightly to keep the edge crisp.
Bánh xèo tôm nhảy Quy Nhơn cỡ nhỏ, vỏ và: Small Quy Nhon bánh xèo with crisp golden shells, earth shrimp and bean sprouts, served with fresh greens; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 55 phút, gồm thời gian để bột ngh: About 55 minutes including resting the batter and cooking the pancakes in batches.
bánh xèo tôm nhảy Quy Nhơn: Quy Nhon bánh xèo tôm nhảy
Bột chỉ cần phủ một lớp mỏng trên chảo n: Spread only a thin layer of batter in a small pan; cover briefly so the shrimp cooks, then uncover to release steam and crisp the shell.
Tôm phải ráo nước trước khi cho vào chảo: Pat the shrimp dry before adding it to the pan to prevent splatter and soggy batter.
Dùng lửa vừa và chờ mép bánh chuyển vàng: Cook over medium heat and wait for the edges to turn golden and release before folding or removing the pancake.
Sift to keep the batter smooth.
Thêm từ từ đến khi bột loãng vừa, bám mỏ: Add gradually until the batter coats the pan thinly.
Use just enough for a light golden color.
Rửa nhanh, bỏ đầu nhọn và để thật ráo; c: Rinse, trim sharp heads and drain thoroughly; small shrimp may retain their thin shells.
Finely slice and mix into the batter.
Use a little for each pancake.
Khuấy bột gạo, bột nghệ và muối với nước: Whisk rice flour, turmeric and salt with water until smooth. Stir in scallions, rest for 10 minutes and stir again.
Rửa tôm, bỏ phần đầu nhọn và thấm thật k: Rinse the shrimp, trim sharp heads and pat thoroughly dry. Wash and drain the bean sprouts, lettuce and herbs.
Pha nước mắm với đường và nước ấm; khi đ: Dissolve the sugar in warm water and fish sauce; once dissolved, add lime, garlic and chili. Taste before serving.
Làm nóng chảo nhỏ ở lửa vừa, thêm một th: Heat a small pan over medium heat and add a teaspoon of oil. Pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl to coat the base thinly.
Xếp vài con tôm và một ít giá lên một nử: Arrange a few shrimp and a little bean sprout over one half of the pancake. Cover for 1–2 minutes until the shrimp is cooked, then uncover to let steam escape.
Rưới một ít dầu quanh viền, tiếp tục chi: Drizzle a little oil around the edge and continue cooking until the edge is crisp and releases from the pan. Fold gently or transfer the pancake whole to a plate.
Lặp lại cho đến hết bột và nhân. Dọn nga: Repeat with the remaining batter and filling. Serve immediately with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
Bún hến Cồn Hến Huế: Hue Cồn Hến mixed clam vermicelli
Bún hến Huế là tô bún trộn với hến xào,: Hue bún hến is a mixed bowl of rice vermicelli with sautéed clams, fresh herbs, peanuts, rice crackers and fermented shrimp paste; hot clam broth is commonly served on the side. Bếp Việt adapts a family version with fresh clams, keeping the savory, spicy flavor while serving shrimp paste and chili separately for individual seasoning.
Bốn tô bún trộn hến; nước luộc hến nóng: Four bowls of mixed vermicelli with clams; hot clam broth is served separately for pouring as desired.
Tô bún trộn có hến xào thơm, rau sống và: A bowl of vermicelli topped with fragrant clams, herbs and banana blossom, finished with peanuts, sesame and pork crackling; served with hot clam broth and chili shrimp paste on the side.
Chia bún vào tô, xếp hến xào và rau lên: Divide vermicelli among bowls and top with sautéed clams and greens. Sprinkle with peanuts, sesame and crackling. Serve with hot clam broth; add shrimp paste or chili to taste and mix before eating.
Bún hến trộn Huế với hến xào, rau sống,: Hue mixed clam vermicelli with sautéed clams, fresh herbs, banana blossom, peanuts and crackling, served with hot clam broth and chili shrimp paste; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 20 phút, gồm 30 phút ngâm h: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 30 minutes to soak the clams and release grit.
Ngâm hến trong nước sạch có chút muối để: Soak clams in clean water with a little salt to release sand, changing the water several times; discard cracked or foul-smelling shells.
Luộc đến khi hến mở miệng, bỏ những con: Boil until shells open and discard any that remain closed; strain the cooking liquid finely to remove grit.
Rau sống và bắp chuối cần rửa kỹ, để thậ: Wash and drain the greens and banana blossom thoroughly; mix them in just before serving to keep their crunch.
Ngâm và thay nước vài lần; bỏ con nứt vỡ: Soak and change the water several times; discard cracked shells.
Soak in diluted lime water, rinse and drain.
Wash, drain thoroughly and roughly chop.
Crush coarsely rather than grinding to powder.
Tóp mỡ hoặc bì heo chiên giòn: Pork crackling or crispy pork skin
Use a moderate amount for savory crunch.
Finely mince for sautéing the clams.
Hòa tan với ít nước luộc hến, nếm trước: Dilute with clam broth and taste before adding.
Add to the clam broth if needed.
Serve separately to adjust the heat.
Ngâm hến trong thau nước sạch có chút mu: Soak the clams in clean water with a little salt for 30 minutes, change the water once and rinse several times to remove grit.
Bào mỏng bắp chuối, ngâm trong nước chan: Shred the banana blossom and soak it in diluted lime water, then rinse. Wash and drain the herbs; crush the peanuts coarsely.
Băm hành tím, sả và ớt. Pha mắm ruốc với: Mince the shallots, lemongrass and chili. Dilute the fermented shrimp paste with a little clam broth and strain if gritty.
Chần bún nhanh bằng nước sôi, xả ráo. Ra: Briefly blanch the vermicelli and drain. Toast the sesame if needed and prepare the crackling or crispy pork skin.
Cho hến vào nồi với lượng nước vừa đủ, đ: Put the clams in a pot with just enough water and bring to a boil until most shells open. Turn off the heat, remove the clams and discard any that remain closed.
Lọc nước luộc qua rây lót vải sạch để gi: Strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve lined with clean cloth to remove sand. Bring the broth back to a boil, season very lightly and keep hot for serving.
Phi thơm hành tím và sả, cho thịt hến và: Sauté shallots and lemongrass until fragrant, add the clam meat and stir-fry briefly. Add some diluted shrimp paste, taste for a savory balance and turn off the heat.
Cho bún vào tô, xếp hến, bắp chuối và ra: Place vermicelli in bowls and arrange clams, banana blossom and herbs on top. Sprinkle with peanuts, sesame and crackling; serve with the hot clam broth and remaining shrimp paste.
Gà Tiên Yên nổi tiếng với thịt thơm ngọt: Tiên Yên chicken is known for fragrant, sweet meat, a firm bite and naturally golden skin. Bếp Việt keeps the preparation simple so the chicken remains the focus, adding a little ginger, shallot and lime leaf. Serve warm with lime-pepper salt or ginger dipping sauce.
Một con gà khoảng 1,4 kg, chặt thành 8–1: One chicken weighing about 1.4 kg, cut into 8–10 pieces and shared by four people.
Gà chín tới, thịt trắng ẩm và săn, da và: The chicken is just cooked, with moist, firm white meat and glossy golden skin; cut into serving pieces and finish with finely sliced lime leaf and lime-pepper salt.
Để gà nghỉ vài phút rồi chặt qua khớp, x: Let the chicken rest briefly, cut through the joints and arrange on a platter with lime leaf. Serve warm with salt, pepper and lime; the cooking broth can be seasoned and served as soup.
Gà luộc Tiên Yên da vàng tự nhiên, chặt: Tiên Yên boiled chicken with naturally golden skin, cut into pieces and served with lime leaf and a small bowl of lime-pepper salt; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 15 phút, gồm 45 phút luộc v: About 1 hour 15 minutes, including 45 minutes of simmering and a 10-minute rest; timing depends on the chicken's size.
Chọn gà Tiên Yên có nguồn gốc rõ ràng; n: Choose traceable Tiên Yên chicken. If it is unavailable, use a similarly sized free-range chicken to keep a firm texture.
Giữ nồi sôi lăn tăn thay vì sôi mạnh để: Keep the pot at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil so the skin is less likely to split and the meat cooks evenly. Timing depends on the bird's size and age.
Dùng nhiệt kế thực phẩm kiểm tra phần dà: Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C. Rest the chicken in the hot broth for about 10 minutes before cutting.
Chọn gà có nguồn gốc rõ ràng; để nguyên: Choose traceable poultry and keep it whole for boiling.
Use a pot deep enough to mostly cover the chicken.
Cho vào nước luộc; gia giảm theo khẩu vị: Season the cooking water; adjust to taste.
Một phần cho vào nồi, phần còn lại thái: Add some to the pot and finely slice the rest for serving.
Add to the salt and pepper at the end.
Optional; mince for the dipping salt.
Kiểm tra khoang bụng, bỏ phần lòng chưa: Check the cavity and remove any uncleaned giblets. Rinse the chicken under clean running water and pat dry. Keep raw poultry away from ready-to-eat foods and clean the sink after preparation.
Đập dập gừng, hành khô; rửa lá chanh. Vắ: Crush the ginger and shallot and rinse the lime leaves. Mix coarse salt with pepper and lime juice; add minced chili if desired.
Cho nước, gừng, hành và muối vào nồi sâu: Put the water, ginger, shallot and salt in a deep pot. Bring to a boil, lower to a gentle simmer and carefully add the chicken.
Luộc lửa nhỏ khoảng 35–45 phút tùy kích: Simmer for about 35–45 minutes depending on size, turning the chicken once. Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C; do not rely on skin color alone.
Tắt bếp, đậy nắp và để gà nghỉ trong nướ: Turn off the heat, cover and let the chicken rest in the hot water for 10 minutes. Lift it out to drain, rest briefly, then cut through the joints and finish with finely sliced lime leaf.
Dọn gà còn ấm cùng muối tiêu chanh. Lọc: Serve warm with lime-pepper salt. Strain and season the cooking broth as soup if desired.
Bánh tét lá cẩm Bình Thủy có lớp nếp tím: Bình Thủy bánh tét lá cẩm has naturally purple sticky rice wrapped around mung beans, pork and salted duck egg yolk. Bếp Việt adapts a one-roll family batch, coloring the rice with magenta-leaf infusion, mixing it with coconut milk, then wrapping it in banana leaves and simmering until fully cooked.
Một đòn bánh cỡ vừa, cắt khoảng 16 khoan: One medium roll, cut into about 16 slices; serve two slices per person as a main or side.
Khoanh bánh có vành nếp tím dẻo, nhân đậ: Each slice has a chewy violet rice layer around yellow mung beans, tender pork and salted egg yolk; the cross-section is round and holds together without becoming mushy.
Để bánh nguội bớt rồi dùng dao sắc cắt k: Let the roll cool slightly, then use a sharp knife to cut slices about 1.5 cm thick. Serve as a light meal or pan-sear both sides for a fragrant, lightly crisp surface.
Bánh tét lá cẩm Cần Thơ với lớp nếp tím,: Cần Thơ magenta-leaf bánh tét with violet rice, mung bean, pork and salted egg filling, sliced on a plate; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 9 giờ 30 phút, gồm 4 giờ ngâm nếp: About 9 hours 30 minutes, including 4 hours of rice soaking and 4 hours 30 minutes of boiling; soak the rice overnight if convenient.
bánh tét nhân thịt trứng muối: bánh tét with pork and salted egg
Ngâm nếp trong nước lá cẩm đã lọc để màu: Soak the rice in strained magenta-leaf water for an even color; drain it thoroughly before mixing in coconut milk.
Gói chặt nhưng chừa chỗ cho nếp nở. Bọc: Wrap firmly but leave room for the rice to expand. Seal the banana-leaf ends so cooking water does not enter the filling.
Trong suốt thời gian luộc, giữ bánh ngập: Keep the roll submerged throughout boiling and top up with hot water. Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate.
Vo sạch, ngâm trong nước lá cẩm 3–4 giờ: Rinse, soak in magenta-leaf infusion for 3–4 hours and drain.
Rửa sạch, nấu lấy nước màu rồi lọc bỏ bã: Rinse, simmer to make purple cooking water and strain.
Dùng nấu lá cẩm; có thể cần thêm nước để: For the leaf infusion and soaking the rice.
Mix into the soaked and drained rice.
Divide between the rice and filling.
Cut into long strips the length of the roll.
Rinse and pat dry; place lengthwise in the filling.
Season the pork; adjust to taste.
Wipe clean and briefly soften over heat; use intact leaves.
Rửa lá cẩm, vò nhẹ rồi nấu với nước 15 p: Rinse and lightly crush the magenta leaves. Simmer them in water for 15 minutes until the liquid is deep purple, strain out the leaves and cool. Rinse the rice, soak it in the infusion for 3–4 hours, then drain thoroughly.
Ngâm đậu xanh 2 giờ, hấp chín và nghiền: Soak the mung beans for two hours, steam until soft and mash coarsely. Season the pork with shallot, fish sauce, pepper and some of the salt; pan-cook until browned and cooked through.
Hơ lá chuối cho mềm và lau khô. Trộn nếp: Soften and dry the banana leaves. Mix the drained rice with coconut milk, sugar and the remaining salt; set out the beans, pork and salted egg yolks for wrapping.
Trải lá chuối thành nhiều lớp, dàn một l: Lay several banana leaves in overlapping layers. Spread rice, add mung beans, pork and egg yolk in the center, then cover with rice. Roll tightly into a cylinder, fold the ends and tie evenly.
Lót lá chuối dưới đáy nồi lớn, đặt bánh: Line a large pot with banana leaves, add the roll and cover with boiling water. Simmer for about 4–4.5 hours, checking often and adding boiling water to keep the roll submerged.
Vớt bánh, rửa nhanh mặt lá bằng nước sạc: Lift out the roll, briefly rinse the leaf exterior with clean water and hang or tilt it to drain. Let it cool and set before removing the ties and slicing with a clean knife.
Bánh tráng phơi sương cuốn thịt luộc Trả: Trảng Bàng dew-wetted rice paper rolls with boiled pork
Món cuốn Trảng Bàng kết hợp bánh tráng p: Trảng Bàng's signature rolls pair soft, pliable dew-wetted rice paper with boiled pork, fresh rice vermicelli and a generous selection of greens, especially local forest herbs. Bếp Việt adapts an easy home platter with familiar herbs and pineapple fermented-fish sauce for a savory, fresh balance.
Khoảng 16 cuốn vừa, dùng chung như bữa c: About 16 medium rolls, served as a shared main meal for four.
Bánh tráng dẻo cuốn vừa tay với thịt heo: Pliable rice paper wraps boiled pork, vermicelli and greens without tearing; serve with pineapple fermented-fish sauce balanced between salty, sweet and sour.
Bày riêng bánh tráng, thịt, bún, rau và: Arrange the rice paper, pork, vermicelli, herbs and vegetables separately so everyone can roll their own. Dew-wetted rice paper is usually ready to use without dipping in water.
Bánh tráng phơi sương Trảng Bàng cuốn th: Trảng Bàng dew-wetted rice paper rolls with boiled pork, vermicelli, herbs and cucumber, served with fermented-fish sauce; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 55 phút để sơ chế rau, luộc thịt: About 55 minutes to prepare the greens, boil the pork and make the dipping sauce; assemble the rolls at the table.
bánh tráng rau rừng Tây Ninh: Tây Ninh rice paper and forest herbs
Bánh tráng phơi sương đã mềm dẻo thì khô: Do not soak pliable dew-wetted rice paper. Keep unused sheets covered so they do not dry out.
Luộc thịt từ nước lạnh để phần giữa chín: Start the pork in cold water for even cooking. Check the thickest piece with a food thermometer; it should reach at least 71°C before slicing.
Rửa rau nhiều lần dưới vòi nước sạch và: Wash the greens thoroughly under clean running water and drain well. Add fermented-fish sauce gradually because saltiness varies by brand.
Chọn bánh dẻo, còn nguyên; thường không: Choose pliable, intact sheets; they usually do not need to be dipped in water.
Chọn miếng có nạc và mỡ xen đều, rửa sạc: Choose a piece with balanced meat and fat and rinse it clean.
Briefly blanch if needed and drain.
Có thể phối xà lách, tía tô, húng quế, d: Use lettuce, perilla, basil, fish mint and seasonal forest herbs.
Rinse and cut into long sticks.
Để ráo; có thể thay bằng rau củ muối chu: Drain well; lightly pickled vegetables also work.
Chọn loại dùng làm nước chấm, gia giảm t: Use a dipping-sauce variety and adjust to its saltiness.
Băm nhuyễn một nửa, phần còn lại có thể: Finely chop half; juice the rest if desired.
Season the sauce, adjusting for the sweetness of the pineapple.
Crush and add to the pork cooking water.
Rửa rau sống nhiều lần dưới vòi nước sạc: Wash the greens several times under clean running water and drain completely. Cut the cucumber and arrange the vermicelli, pickled vegetables and rice paper separately on a platter.
Rửa thịt, cho vào nồi nước lạnh cùng gừn: Rinse the pork and place it in a pot of cold water with crushed ginger and salt. Mince the pineapple, garlic and chili; set out the fermented-fish sauce, sugar and warm water.
Đun nồi thịt đến sôi, hớt bọt rồi hạ lửa: Bring the pork to a boil, skim the foam and lower the heat to a gentle simmer for about 20–25 minutes depending on thickness. Check that the center reaches at least 71°C with a food thermometer; cool before slicing thinly.
Cho mắm nêm, thơm băm, tỏi, đường và nướ: Combine fermented-fish sauce, chopped pineapple, garlic, sugar and warm water in a small saucepan. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, taste and add chili; let it cool slightly before serving.
Xếp bánh tráng phơi sương, thịt, bún, ra: Arrange the rice paper, pork, vermicelli, herbs, cucumber and pickled vegetables on a platter. Roll each serving just before eating and dip in the sauce.
Bánh bèo chén Cẩm Kim Hội An: Cẩm Kim Hội An bánh bèo rice cakes
Bánh bèo Cẩm Kim là món ăn dân dã của Hộ: Cẩm Kim bánh bèo is a rustic Hội An breakfast, prepared in the Quảng Nam style with thicker, soft rice cakes and a minced shrimp-and-pork topping. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch steamed in small bowls, finished with scallion oil and fried shallots and served with mildly spicy fish sauce.
Khoảng 16 chén nhỏ, 4 chén mỗi người; dù: About 16 small bowls, four per person; serve hot with seasoned fish sauce.
Chén bánh trắng đục, mặt bánh mềm dày vừ: Small bowls of opaque white rice cake with a soft, moderately thick texture, topped with orange-brown minced shrimp and pork, fried shallots and scallion oil; serve with fish sauce on the side or spooned over.
Dọn bánh ngay sau khi hấp, thêm nhưn nón: Serve the cakes as soon as they come out of the steamer, topped with hot shrimp-and-pork mixture, scallion oil and fried shallots. Add a little fish sauce to each bowl or serve it on the side.
Các chén bánh bèo Cẩm Kim Hội An với như: Small bowls of Cẩm Kim Hội An bánh bèo topped with minced shrimp and pork, scallion oil and fried shallots on a ceramic tray; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 10 phút, gồm 20 phút để bột: About 1 hour 10 minutes, including 20 minutes for the batter to rest and steaming in batches.
bánh bèo chén nhân tôm thịt: bánh bèo with minced shrimp and pork
Khuấy lại bột trước khi rót vì bột gạo d: Stir the batter again before pouring because rice flour settles. A moderate layer lets the cakes steam evenly in small bowls.
Hấp chén trước cho nóng để mặt bánh mịn;: Preheat the empty bowls in the steamer so the batter sets smoothly; avoid opening the lid repeatedly while the cakes cook.
Nhân tôm thịt Quảng Nam được nêm vừa để: Season the Quảng Nam-style shrimp-and-pork topping lightly so the shrimp's sweetness remains clear; adjust the fish sauce at the table.
Giúp mặt bánh dai nhẹ; có thể giảm nếu t: Adds a light chew; use less for a softer cake.
Whisk into the flour gradually to prevent lumps.
Mince finely and retain a little fat so the topping stays moist.
Divide between the topping and scallion oil.
For the dipping sauce; adjust to taste.
Optional; mince for the dipping sauce.
Scatter over the cakes before serving.
Hòa bột gạo, bột năng, muối và nước đến: Whisk rice flour, tapioca starch, salt and water until smooth. Rest for 20 minutes, then stir again; prepare 16 clean small bowls and a steamer.
Băm tôm, thịt và hành tím. Thái hành lá,: Mince the shrimp, pork and shallot. Slice the scallions. Mix fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, warm water and chili to taste for the dipping sauce.
Đặt chén rỗng vào xửng hấp cho nóng. Khu: Set the empty bowls in the steamer to warm. Stir the batter, fill each bowl halfway to two-thirds and steam for 7–9 minutes until the cakes turn opaque and the surface is just set.
Trong lúc hấp bánh, phi hành tím với một: While the cakes steam, fry the shallot in some of the oil until fragrant. Add the pork and cook through, then add the shrimp and fish sauce; stir-fry until the topping is fully cooked and lightly moist.
Rưới phần dầu còn ấm vào hành lá. Múc nh: Warm the remaining oil and pour it over the scallions. Spoon the topping onto each cake, add scallion oil and fried shallots, then serve hot with seasoned fish sauce.
Canh lá mì cà đắng cá khô Tây Nguyên: Central Highlands cassava-leaf soup with bitter eggplant and dried fish
Canh lá mì là món rau rừng quen thuộc tr: Cassava-leaf soup is an everyday forest-vegetable dish in many Central Highlands communities. Young cassava leaves are pounded and simmered with bitter eggplant and dried fish, creating a nutty, gently bitter flavor associated with the highlands. Bếp Việt adapts a home version and emphasizes careful processing of the leaves before they enter the pot.
Một nồi canh khoảng 1,4 lít, chia 4 bát: About 1.4 liters of soup, divided among four bowls and served with steamed rice.
Lá mì mềm nhừ trong nước canh xanh nâu,: Soft cassava leaves simmer in a green-brown broth with intact pieces of bitter eggplant and lightly smoky dried fish; the flavor is gently bitter, nutty and moderately salty.
Múc canh nóng vào bát, dùng cùng cơm trắ: Ladle the soup hot into bowls and serve with steamed rice. Taste for salt only after the dried fish has released its flavor; serve fresh chili separately if desired.
Bát canh lá mì Tây Nguyên nấu cà đắng và: A bowl of Central Highlands cassava-leaf soup with bitter eggplant and dried fish, the leaves tender in a green-brown broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 5 phút, gồm sơ chế lá mì kỹ: About 1 hour 5 minutes, including careful leaf preparation, a separate brief boil and a second simmer until fully tender.
Chỉ dùng lá sắn non được bán làm thực ph: Use only young cassava leaves sold for food and process them safely; raw cassava leaves contain cyanogenic compounds.
Giã dập lá ít nhất 10 phút, rửa với lượn: Pound the leaves thoroughly for at least 10 minutes, wash them with plenty of clean water, boil separately for 8–10 minutes and discard all the cooking water. Then simmer them in the soup until very tender.
Cá khô vốn mặn nên rửa nhanh, nướng sơ v: Dried fish is already salty, so rinse it briefly, toast it and add fish sauce only at the end. Reduce the bitter eggplant if diners are new to its flavor.
Lá mì non đã sơ chế làm thực phẩm: Young cassava leaves prepared as food
Chỉ dùng lá non có nguồn gốc thực phẩm;: Use only food-grade young leaves; pound, wash, boil separately and discard that water before making the soup.
Chọn cá khô ăn được, rửa nhanh và nướng: Choose edible dried fish, rinse briefly and toast; check for bones before eating.
Gồm nước nấu canh; dùng thêm nước riêng: For the soup; use separate additional water to wash and boil the leaves, then discard it.
Có thể bỏ qua nếu muốn nấu theo cách mộc: Optional; omit for a more rustic preparation.
Add at the end because dried fish is salty.
Add only if the broth still needs seasoning.
Optional; slice and serve on the side.
Nhặt lá mì non, bỏ cuống già. Giã dập th: Pick young cassava leaves and remove tough stems. Pound thoroughly for at least 10 minutes, wash with plenty of clean water and change the water. Boil the leaves separately for 8–10 minutes and discard all of that water. Do not taste raw leaves or use leaves of uncertain origin.
Rửa cá khô nhanh, nướng hoặc áp chảo sơ: Briefly rinse the dried fish, toast it and remove large bones. Rinse the bitter eggplant; crush the lemongrass, shallot and garlic.
Đun nóng dầu, phi hành tím, tỏi và sả đế: Heat the oil and fry the shallot, garlic and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the dried fish and stir briefly to release its aroma.
Đổ nước vào nồi, đun sôi nhẹ rồi cho lá: Pour in the soup water and bring to a gentle boil. Add the pre-boiled, drained cassava leaves and bitter eggplant. Lower the heat and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the leaves are very soft.
Nêm nước mắm và chỉ thêm muối khi cần. Đ: Season with fish sauce and add salt only if needed. Simmer for a few more minutes, check that the leaves are fully tender and the eggplant is cooked, then serve hot with steamed rice.
Coóng phù là món bánh nếp viên tròn gắn: Coóng phù is a round glutinous-rice dumpling associated with the Tày community in Cao Bằng and is often enjoyed hot in cold weather. Bếp Việt adapts a home version using glutinous-rice flour, ginger and sugarcane molasses; the dumplings are boiled separately before being served in the syrup so it stays clear and fragrant.
Một bát nhỏ coóng phù nóng cho mỗi người: Four small bowls of hot coóng phù, served as an afternoon treat or winter dessert.
Những viên bánh nếp trắng dẻo nằm trong: Soft white rice dumplings sit in amber sugarcane-molasses syrup with warming ginger and a light sprinkle of toasted sesame; the syrup remains clear rather than cloudy.
Chia bánh và nước mật gừng vào bát nhỏ k: Divide the dumplings and hot ginger-molasses syrup among small bowls. Add toasted sesame or crushed peanuts if desired and serve while warm.
Bát coóng phù Cao Bằng với viên bánh nếp: A bowl of Cao Bằng coóng phù: soft white rice dumplings in amber ginger and sugarcane-molasses syrup, finished with toasted sesame; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 40 phút, gồm nhào bột, luộc bánh: About 40 minutes to knead the dough, boil the dumplings and prepare the ginger-molasses syrup.
Rót nước ấm từ từ vào bột; dừng khi khối: Add warm water gradually until the dough is smooth, pliable and no longer sticky.
Luộc bánh riêng trong nước sôi, vớt khi: Boil the dumplings separately, remove them when they float, then add them to the ginger syrup to keep the syrup clear.
Mật mía có độ ngọt khác nhau; hòa loãng: Molasses sweetness varies; dilute and taste it before adding extra sugar.
Rây qua để bột tơi; dùng bột nếp mới để: Sift before mixing; fresh flour gives a tender, chewy texture.
Cho từ từ, lượng thực tế phụ thuộc độ hú: Add gradually; the amount depends on the flour's absorption.
Có thể thay bằng đường phên nấu chảy; nế: Palm sugar may be used; taste before adjusting.
Rửa sạch, đập dập; giữ lại vài lát mỏng: Crush it and reserve a few thin slices for serving.
Cho bột nếp và muối vào âu. Rót nước ấm: Combine the glutinous-rice flour and salt. Gradually add warm water and knead for 6–8 minutes until smooth, pliable and not sticky. Cover for 10 minutes.
Chia bột thành viên nhỏ cỡ đầu ngón tay: Roll the dough into small balls about the size of a large marble and place them on a dry tray. Crush the ginger and combine the molasses with the syrup water.
Đun nồi nước riêng sôi nhẹ. Thả bánh từn: Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil. Add the dumplings in batches and stir once. When they float, cook for about 1 more minute, then lift them out to drain.
Đun nước mật mía cùng gừng và muối ở lửa: Simmer the molasses, water, ginger and salt over low heat for 5–7 minutes until fragrant. Taste and adjust; do not reduce it to a candy-like syrup.
Cho bánh đã luộc vào nồi nước mật, hâm t: Add the cooked dumplings to the ginger syrup and warm for 1–2 minutes. Ladle into bowls, add sesame and serve hot.
Thắng dền là món bánh nếp viên nhỏ của H: Thắng dền is a small glutinous-rice dumpling from Hà Giang, commonly filled with mung bean and served in hot ginger-sugar syrup. Bếp Việt prepares a home-style version with a light coconut-milk drizzle, roasted peanuts and shredded coconut; adjust the sweetness to taste.
Bốn bát nhỏ, mỗi bát 5–6 viên bánh nếp n: Four small bowls, each with 5–6 mung-bean-filled rice dumplings in ginger syrup.
Viên bánh nếp trắng ngà, một vài viên hé: Ivory rice dumplings, some showing their golden mung-bean filling, sit in hot ginger syrup with a restrained coconut-milk drizzle, roasted peanuts and coconut.
Chia bánh và nước gừng vào bát, rưới một: Divide the dumplings and ginger syrup among bowls. Drizzle with warm coconut milk, add crushed peanuts and shredded coconut, and serve while hot.
Bát thắng dền Hà Giang gồm viên bánh nếp: A bowl of Hà Giang thắng dền: mung-bean-filled rice dumplings in ginger syrup with a light coconut-milk drizzle and roasted peanuts; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ, gồm hấp nhân, nặn bánh và: About 1 hour, including steaming the filling, shaping the dumplings and cooking the ginger syrup.
Để nhân đậu xanh nguội hẳn trước khi bọc: Cool the mung-bean filling completely before wrapping; keep each filling ball smaller than its dough wrapper.
Nhào bột đến khi mềm dẻo nhưng không nhã: Knead until pliable but not wet; if the dough cracks, moisten your hands instead of pouring in a lot of water.
Nấu nước đường gừng ở lửa nhỏ và nếm trư: Keep the ginger syrup at a gentle simmer and add the coconut milk only when serving so the ginger remains distinct.
Add gradually depending on the flour.
Ngâm 2 giờ, hấp hoặc nấu chín mềm rồi ng: Soak for 2 hours, rinse, then steam or cook until soft and mash.
Break into small pieces so it dissolves quickly.
Crush it; reserve a few slices for serving.
Divide between the dough and filling.
Ngâm đậu xanh 2 giờ, xả sạch rồi hấp chí: Soak the mung beans for 2 hours, rinse and steam until soft. Mash while warm with the granulated sugar and a pinch of salt. Cool and roll into 20–24 small balls.
Trộn bột nếp với phần muối còn lại. Rót: Mix the remaining salt into the glutinous-rice flour. Add warm water gradually and knead until smooth and pliable; divide into 20–24 portions.
Ấn dẹt từng phần bột, đặt nhân đậu xanh: Flatten each dough portion, place a mung-bean ball in the center, seal completely and roll smooth. Set the dumplings on a dry tray without touching.
Đun đường phên với nước và gừng đập dập: Simmer the palm sugar, water and crushed ginger over low heat for about 8 minutes until dissolved and fragrant. Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Đun một nồi nước riêng sôi nhẹ. Thả bánh: Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil. Cook the dumplings in batches; when they float, cook for 1–2 minutes more, then transfer them into the ginger syrup.
Hâm bánh trong nước đường thêm 2 phút. C: Warm the dumplings in the syrup for 2 minutes. Divide into bowls, drizzle with warm coconut milk, add peanuts and coconut, and serve hot.
Mì Quảng ếch là một biến thể quen thuộc: Mì Quảng ếch is a familiar variation of Đà Nẵng mì Quảng. Frog is marinated and braised with lemongrass, củ nén and turmeric to make a fragrant, concentrated topping. Bếp Việt adapts a home version with just enough broth to moisten the wide noodles, served with fresh herbs, roasted peanuts and sesame rice crackers.
Bốn tô mì Quảng với khoảng 150 g mì tươi: Four bowls with about 150 g fresh noodles and 2–3 pieces of braised frog per serving, with herbs and rice crackers.
Sợi mì vàng nghệ dai mềm, phủ phần ếch o: Chewy golden turmeric noodles are topped with glossy lemongrass-and-turmeric braised frog and a little concentrated broth; peanuts, fresh herbs and crisp sesame rice crackers add texture.
Xếp mì vào tô, đặt ếch và phần nhưn lên: Place the noodles in bowls, top with frog and a little concentrated broth rather than filling the bowl. Serve with fresh herbs, lime, chili, roasted peanuts and sesame rice crackers.
Tô mì Quảng ếch Đà Nẵng với sợi mì vàng,: A bowl of Đà Nẵng mì Quảng ếch with golden noodles, lemongrass-and-turmeric braised frog, herbs, peanuts and sesame rice crackers; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 10 phút, gồm ướp nhanh, om: About 1 hour 10 minutes, including marinating, braising and preparing the fresh herbs.
Chọn đùi ếch đã sơ chế ở cơ sở uy tín; t: Choose cleaned frog legs from a reputable supplier, pat dry before marinating, and cook fully; keep raw marinade away from ready-to-eat herbs.
Củ nén (hành tăm) cho mùi đặc trưng; nếu: Củ nén, also called hành tăm, gives a distinctive aroma; shallots can replace it if needed, though the flavor will differ.
Nấu phần nhưn hơi đậm và sánh; mì Quảng: Keep the topping broth concentrated and use only a small amount in each bowl.
Mua tại cơ sở uy tín, giữ lạnh và nấu ch: Buy from a reputable supplier, keep chilled and cook thoroughly.
Sợi bản rộng; trụng nhanh nếu mì cần làm: Wide rice noodles; warm briefly if needed.
Dùng vừa đủ nấu nhưn, không chan ngập tô: Use enough for a concentrated topping, not a full soup bowl.
Bóc vỏ, đập dập; có thể thay một phần bằ: Peel and crush; shallot may replace part of it.
Mince half and bruise the rest.
Giã hoặc xay nhuyễn; dùng găng để tránh: Grate or blend; wear gloves to avoid staining.
Neutral cooking oil can be used instead.
Divide between the marinade and broth.
A small amount balances the seasoning.
Rau cải non, giá, rau thơm và bắp chuối: Young mustard greens, bean sprouts, herbs and banana blossom; wash carefully and drain.
Kiểm tra đùi ếch đã được sơ chế sạch; th: Check the cleaned frog legs, pat dry and cut into serving pieces. Marinate with half the fish sauce, turmeric, pepper, some of the củ nén and minced lemongrass for 15 minutes; refrigerate if not cooking immediately.
Rinse the fresh herbs under clean running water and drain. Prepare the roasted peanuts, rice crackers, lime, chili and scallions; keep them separate from the raw frog.
Làm nóng dầu phụng, phi thơm phần củ nén: Heat the peanut oil and sauté the remaining củ nén and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the marinated frog and stir until the surface firms.
Thêm nước dùng, đường và phần nước mắm c: Add the broth, sugar and remaining fish sauce. Cover and braise gently for 18–22 minutes until the frog is fully cooked and the broth lightly thickens; taste and adjust.
Warm the noodles according to their package instructions. Divide into bowls, add the frog and a small amount of broth, then finish with scallions and peanuts. Serve with herbs, crackers, lime and chili.
Lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua Hậu Giang: Hậu Giang fish-cake and bitter-melon hotpot
Lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua kết hợp cá thát: Lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua pairs the springy, sweet fish of Hậu Giang with the clean bitterness of bitter melon. Bếp Việt adapts a home hotpot with pork-bone broth, daikon and mushrooms; the fish is kneaded into tender balls and added near serving time.
Một nồi lẩu nhỏ cho bốn người, ăn kèm bú: One small hotpot for four people, served with fresh rice vermicelli or steamed rice.
Nồi nước dùng trong và ngọt xương, viên: A clear, savory broth holds ivory fish-cake balls and bright green bitter-melon slices; scallions and a little chili add aroma, while the bitterness remains gentle on the finish.
Đun nồi lẩu liu riu trên bàn, thả khổ qu: Keep the hotpot at a gentle simmer and add bitter melon and other vegetables in small batches to keep them fresh. Serve with rice vermicelli, fish sauce and chili, or steamed rice.
Nồi lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua Hậu Giang vớ: Hậu Giang fish-cake and bitter-melon hotpot with springy ivory fish balls, green bitter-melon slices and clear broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 1 giờ 25 phút, gồm hầm nước dùng: About 1 hour 25 minutes, including simmering the pork-bone broth and preparing the fish balls.
cá thát lát nấu lẩu: lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua
Nếu mua cá xay sẵn, kiểm tra nguồn lạnh: If using pre-ground fish, check the cold chain and ingredients; knead chilled fish in one direction until elastic so the balls hold together.
Nêm nước dùng vừa trước khi thả cá; cá x: Season the broth lightly before adding the fish; ground fish may already be seasoned, so taste again after it cooks.
Cho khổ qua vào gần lúc ăn và không nấu: Add bitter melon shortly before serving and avoid overcooking to preserve its green color and gentle bitterness.
Dùng cá nạo tươi, giữ lạnh; kiểm tra xươ: Use freshly scraped chilled fish; check for small bones and a reliable source.
Bổ dọc, bỏ ruột và thái lát dày khoảng 5: Halve lengthwise, remove the pith and slice about 5 mm thick.
For the broth; top up with boiling water if needed.
Thái nhỏ, trộn một phần vào cá và phần c: Season the broth and fish; adjust for the saltiness of the fish paste.
Slice; mix some into the fish and save the rest for serving.
Serve separately or add to taste.
Serve on the side; briefly blanch if needed.
Chần xương 3 phút trong nước sôi, đổ nướ: Blanch the pork bones for 3 minutes, discard the water and rinse the bones. Put them in a pot with the daikon, shallots and fresh water; keep chilled if not simmering immediately.
Giữ cá nạo lạnh. Trộn cá với một phần nư: Keep the fish paste cold. Mix it with some fish sauce, pepper and scallions; knead in one direction for 5–7 minutes until sticky and elastic. Shape into bite-size balls and chill while the broth simmers.
Bổ khổ qua, bỏ ruột, thái lát; làm sạch: Halve the bitter melon, remove the pith and slice. Clean the mushrooms and prepare the vermicelli and hotpot greens away from the raw fish-preparation area.
Hầm xương với củ cải ở lửa nhỏ 40–45 phú: Simmer the bones and daikon over low heat for 40–45 minutes, skimming regularly to keep the broth clear. Remove the larger bones if desired, then season with salt and the remaining fish sauce.
Đun sôi nhẹ nồi nước dùng, thả từng viên: Bring the broth to a gentle boil and add the fish balls. Cook for 5–7 minutes until they float and are cooked through; add the mushrooms and cook for 3 more minutes.
Chuyển nồi lên bếp lẩu. Thêm khổ qua từn: Move the pot to the table burner. Add bitter melon in batches and cook until just tender but still green. Finish with scallions and serve with rice vermicelli and fish sauce with chili.
Bánh chưng gù là bánh nếp gói nhỏ bằng t: Bánh chưng gù is a small hand-wrapped sticky-rice cake associated with the Tày people of Hà Giang. Bếp Việt adapts the Ngọc Đường style using rice naturally tinted green with leaf ginger, mung beans and pork belly wrapped in dong leaves and simmered until the rice is tender. It requires advance preparation and long cooking.
Bốn bánh chưng gù cỡ nhỏ, mỗi người một: Four small hunchback-shaped cakes, one per person or halved for a festive meal.
Bánh gói tay nhỏ có dáng gù mềm, lá dong: Small hand-wrapped cakes have a softly curved hunchback shape and deep-green dong leaves; the cut face shows naturally green sticky rice around a savory mung-bean and pork-belly filling.
Để bánh ráo và nguội bớt rồi cắt đôi hoặ: Let the cakes drain and cool slightly before cutting into halves or thick slices. Serve warm with pickled onions or pickled vegetables, or as a filling breakfast during Tết.
Bánh chưng gù Hà Giang gói nhỏ bằng lá d: Small Hà Giang bánh chưng gù wrapped in dong leaves, one cut to show naturally green leaf-ginger rice with mung-bean and pork filling; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
Khoảng 16 giờ, gồm 6 giờ ngâm và 9 giờ l: About 16 hours in total, including 6 hours of soaking and 9 hours of boiling; soak the rice and beans ahead.
Ngâm gạo và đậu riêng; để ráo thật kỹ tr: Soak the rice and mung beans separately; drain them well before wrapping so the cakes cook evenly without becoming wet.
Gói bánh chặt tay theo dáng nhỏ hơi cong: Wrap each cake tightly by hand into a small curved shape, but do not compress the rice so firmly that it cannot expand; tie the leaves securely.
Luộc ngập bánh liên tục 8–10 giờ, châm t: Keep the cakes submerged in water for 8–10 hours and top up with boiling water as needed; never let the pot run dry or expose the cakes.
Vo nhẹ, ngâm 6 giờ rồi để ráo; chọn hạt: Rinse gently, soak for 6 hours and drain; choose fresh sticky rice.
Ngâm riêng 2 giờ, để ráo; có thể hấp sơ: Soak separately for 2 hours and drain; steam briefly for a fluffy filling if desired.
Cut into four long strips for the filling.
Chọn lá mềm, rửa sạch và lau khô; dùng t: Choose flexible leaves, wash and dry; use scraps as extra lining if needed.
Xay với khoảng 100 ml nước, lọc lấy nước: Blend with about 100 ml water and strain to obtain green coloring liquid.

Làm sạch cá suối và chuẩn bị vỉ nướng. R: Clean the stream fish and prepare a grill. Roast the peanuts if needed, then lightly crush them.

Khuấy nước cốt chanh, nước mắm, tỏi, ớt: Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, garlic, chili and a little salt. Place the bamboo, flower petals, fish and herbs in a bowl.
Rưới nước trộn từng ít một, đảo nhẹ cho: Add the dressing gradually and toss gently. Taste, top with roasted peanuts and serve immediately.
Nhứa pho thịt băm gói lá nướng Tây Bắc: Northwest Thai Nhứa Pho Leaf-Wrapped Grilled Pork
Nhứa pho là thịt băm trộn gia vị thơm nh: Nhứa pho is minced pork mixed with fragrant lemongrass, ginger, garlic and mắc khén, wrapped in dong or banana leaves and grilled over charcoal. Bếp Việt divides it into smaller parcels for even cooking while keeping the tender meat and toasted leaf aroma.
Bốn gói thịt nướng, chia ăn cùng cơm hoặ: Four grilled pork parcels, served with rice or upland sticky rice.
Gói lá vàng sậm, bên trong là thịt vai b: Dark-golden leaf parcels hold tender minced pork fragrant with lemongrass, ginger, shallot, garlic and mắc khén; moist inside and not charred.
Dọn nóng cùng cơm trắng hoặc xôi nếp nươ: Serve hot with plain rice or upland sticky rice. Open the parcels at the table and use a clean plate; never return cooked pork to a plate that held raw meat.
Đĩa nhứa pho Tây Bắc gồm gói lá dong nướ: Northwest Thai nhứa pho on a ceramic plate, with a golden grilled dong-leaf parcel opened to show seasoned minced pork; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
About 1 hour, including 15 minutes to marinate the pork.

Gói thịt thành lớp dẹt vừa phải bằng 2–3: Use two or three layers of dong or banana leaves and keep each parcel moderately thin so the center cooks through.
Nướng cách than vừa đủ, lật thường xuyên: Grill a moderate distance from the coals and turn often; ground pork should reach at least 71°C in the center.
Chọn phần có chút mỡ; băm nhỏ bằng dao h: Choose a cut with some fat; mince by hand or grind coarsely.

Season gradually to account for its saltiness.

Trộn thịt với các gia vị và mắc khén, để: Mix the pork with the seasonings and mắc khén, then marinate for 15 minutes. Rinse and dry the dong leaves; cut them to a size suitable for wrapping.
Chia thịt thành bốn phần dẹt. Đặt từng p: Divide the pork into four flat portions. Place each portion on two or three layers of leaves and fold into a sealed rectangle; secure with a toothpick if needed.
Nướng trên vỉ cách than hồng vừa phải kh: Grill over moderately hot coals for about 10–12 minutes per side, turning evenly until the leaves are dark golden but not charred. Alternatively, bake at 200°C for about 20–25 minutes, turning halfway.
Dùng nhiệt kế kiểm tra phần thịt dày nhấ: Check the thickest portion with a food thermometer; it should reach at least 71°C. Rest for 2 minutes, open the parcels and serve hot.
Cá chạch sụn kho niêu Ninh Bình: Ninh Binh soft-bone loach in a claypot
Cá chạch sụn nhỏ để nguyên con, ướp nước: Small soft-bone loaches are kept whole, seasoned with fish sauce, shallot, garlic and pepper, then slowly braised in a claypot until tender, with a thickened sauce and softened bones. Bep Viet adapts the seasoning amounts for a family meal from the method recorded by a cooperative in Yen Hoa, Yen Mo.
Một niêu cá kho nhỏ dùng làm món mặn cho: One small claypot of braised fish as a main dish for four with steamed rice.
Cá nguyên con mềm thấm vị mặn ngọt, thơm: Whole loaches are tender and savory-sweet, fragrant with shallot, garlic and pepper, in a glossy brown sauce reduced just enough to serve with hot rice.
Dọn cá trong niêu còn nóng, rưới phần nư: Serve hot in the claypot, spooning the sauce over the fish. Pair with steamed rice, seasonal boiled greens or pickled vegetables; lift gently to keep the fish whole.
Niêu đất nhỏ đựng cá chạch sụn nguyên co: A small claypot of whole, glossy brown soft-bone loaches braised with shallot, garlic and pepper; original Bep Viet image on transparency.
Khoảng 8 giờ 45 phút, gồm 15 phút ướp và: About 8 hours 45 minutes, including 15 minutes to season and just over 8 hours of gentle braising.
Chọn cá chạch sụn nhỏ, tươi sống; cá nhỏ: Choose fresh, small soft-bone loaches so they soften evenly during the long braise.
Làm sạch nhớt kỹ, giữ cá nguyên con như: Clean away the slime carefully and keep the fish whole, following the local account; season moderately because the sauce reduces.
Đun thật nhỏ và kiểm tra đáy nồi định kỳ: Keep the heat very low and check the pot bottom regularly. Add a little hot water if the sauce is nearly dry before the fish softens.
Chọn cá tươi sống, cỡ nhỏ; để nguyên con: Choose fresh, small fish; keep them whole after cleaning.
Dùng kho và châm thêm từng ít nếu nồi cạ: Use for braising and add a little at a time if the pot dries before the fish softens.
Season lightly because the sauce reduces during the long braise.

Dùng một phần để làm sạch cá, phần còn l: Use some to clean the fish and the rest for seasoning.

Tùy chọn, điều chỉnh theo độ mặn của nướ: Optional; adjust to the saltiness of the fish sauce.
Rửa cá dưới vòi nước, xát nhẹ với muối v: Rinse the loaches under running water. Gently rub with salt and lemon juice to remove slime, rinse again and drain. Keep them whole and use a separate board and utensils for raw fish.
Băm hành khô, tỏi; cân nước mắm, đường,: Mince the shallot and garlic; measure the fish sauce, sugar, pepper and seasoning powder. Warm the claypot gradually to prevent thermal shock.
Trộn cá với nước mắm, hành, tỏi, đường,: Toss the fish with fish sauce, shallot, garlic, sugar, salt, half the pepper and seasoning powder if using. Leave to season for 15 minutes.
Xếp cá thành lớp trong niêu, thêm nước n: Arrange the fish in a single layer in the claypot and add just enough hot water to moisten the bottom. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to its lowest setting and cover.
Kho liu riu khoảng 8 giờ, thỉnh thoảng k: Braise gently for about 8 hours, checking the bottom occasionally and adding a little hot water if needed. Avoid stirring. The fish is ready when tender, the sauce is glossy brown and the small bones have softened like cartilage.
Mở nắp ở cuối để nước kho sánh nhẹ, nếm: Uncover near the end to lightly thicken the sauce. Adjust the sweet-salty balance, add the remaining pepper and serve hot in the claypot.
Chả nem vuông Bồng Hải: Bong Hai square fried spring rolls
Chả Bồng Hải gói nhân thịt vai, mộc nhĩ,: Bong Hai rolls are filled with pork shoulder, wood-ear mushrooms, glass noodles and shredded water spinach, wrapped into squares in rice paper and fried golden. Bep Viet scales the ingredients for a family table based on the Khanh Thien dish documented by Ninh Binh Newspaper.
Khoảng 12 miếng chả vuông làm món mặn ho: About 12 square rolls to share as a main or communal dish for four.
Miếng chả vuông vàng giòn, nhân thịt mềm: Crisp golden square rolls with a tender filling of pork, wood-ear mushrooms, glass noodles and water spinach, served hot with herbs and sweet-sour dipping sauce.
Dọn chả ngay khi còn nóng với rau thơm v: Serve immediately while hot with fresh herbs and sweet-sour fish sauce. Use clean chopsticks to handle the rolls; they also go well with steamed rice as part of a family meal.
Đĩa chả đa vuông Bồng Hải vàng giòn, một: A plate of crisp golden Bong Hai square rice-paper rolls, one cut open to show pork, noodles, wood-ear mushrooms and water spinach; original Bep Viet image on transparency.
Khoảng 1 giờ 5 phút, gồm 15 phút ngâm mi: About 1 hour 5 minutes, including 15 minutes to soak the noodles and mushrooms.
Ngâm mộc nhĩ và miến vừa mềm rồi để thật: Soak the wood-ear mushrooms and noodles only until pliable, then drain thoroughly so the filling stays dry.
Thái rau muống thành sợi mảnh để nhân dễ: Cut the water spinach into fine strands so it fits neatly in the filling and keeps a slight crunch.
Gấp kín bốn góc bánh đa nem; rán từng mẻ: Fold all four corners tightly and fry in batches so the oil stays hot and the rolls brown evenly.

Băm thịt, hành lá và mùi tàu. Đánh tan t: Mince the pork, scallions and culantro. Beat the egg, and rinse and set aside the fresh herbs.

Dọn chả khi còn nóng cùng rau thơm và nư: Serve hot with fresh herbs and sweet-sour dipping sauce.
Giò trứng Nộn Khê: Non Khe Egg and Pork Loaf
Giò trứng Ninh Bình: Ninh Binh egg and pork loaf
Khoanh giò vuông của làng Nộn Khê xếp lớ: This square loaf from Non Khe village layers ground lean pork, pork belly and hard-boiled eggs in banana leaves, then boils and presses the wrapped loaf into shape. Bep Viet edits a smaller family batch while retaining the traditional layered structure and pressing method.

Để giò nguội và lạnh đủ chắc rồi cắt lát: Chill the loaf until firm, then slice. Serve with pickled onions and plain fish sauce. Wrap leftovers tightly and refrigerate promptly.

Chạo chân giò Bồng Hải: Bong Hai Pork Leg Chao Salad
Chạo chân giò Bồng Hải trộn thịt chân gi: Bong Hai pork leg chao combines cooked pork leg with galangal, lemongrass, sour starfruit, lime leaf and sesame, and is wrapped in fig leaves or rice paper. Bep Viet adapts the seasoning for four based on the traditional preparation documented by Ninh Binh Newspaper.
Một đĩa chạo chân giò và rau cuốn cho bố: One platter of pork leg chao with wrapping greens for four at a family meal or feast.
Thịt chân giò mềm, phần bì giòn dai quyệ: Tender pork leg with pleasantly chewy skin, fragrant spicy galangal, tart starfruit and nutty sesame, wrapped in leaves and served with a sweet-sour-salty dip.
Bày chạo với rau thơm, lá sung và bánh đ: Arrange the chao with fresh herbs, fig leaves and rice paper. Wrap small portions and dip in sweet-sour fish sauce or tuong Ban fermented soybean sauce. Serve soon after mixing so the greens stay fresh.
Đĩa chạo chân giò Bồng Hải trộn riềng sả: A plate of Bong Hai pork leg chao mixed with galangal, lemongrass, sour starfruit, lime leaf and sesame, with wrapping leaves; original Bep Viet image on transparency.
Khoảng 1 giờ 20 phút, gồm 10 phút để thị: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 10 minutes for the meat to rest and cool slightly before mixing.

Nêm riềng, khế và nước mắm từ từ; món cầ: Add galangal, starfruit and fish sauce gradually; the dish should be tart, fragrant and gently spicy without masking the pork.

Serve separately and season to taste.

Trộn thịt với riềng, sả, tỏi, khế, lá ch: Toss the pork with the galangal, lemongrass, garlic, starfruit, lime leaves, fish sauce, salt, sugar, pepper and chili if using. Taste and balance the tart, salty and spicy notes.
Rắc vừng rang, đảo nhẹ lần cuối và bày r: Scatter over the toasted sesame and fold gently once more. Plate with fig leaves, fresh herbs, rice paper and dipping sauce.
Bánh đa Khánh Thiện làm từ gạo tẻ không: Khanh Thien rice crackers are made with non-glutinous rice, sesame and salt. The batter is steamed in two thin layers, the crackers are dried until just right, then grilled over charcoal until crisp and airy. Bep Viet adapts the village process to a small home batch; drying time depends on the weather.
Khoảng bốn bánh đa vừng cỡ lớn, mỗi ngườ: About four large sesame crackers, one per person, eaten soon after grilling.
Bánh tròn mỏng, thơm mùi gạo rang và vừn: Thin round crackers with a toasted-rice and sesame aroma, crisp and airy after charcoal grilling, best eaten freshly cooked.
Bẻ bánh thành miếng và ăn ngay khi còn g: Break the cracker into pieces and eat while crisp. Roasted or boiled peanuts are local-style accompaniments.
Bánh đa vừng Khánh Thiện tròn mỏng, nướn: Thin round Khanh Thien sesame rice crackers, grilled golden and covered with sesame seeds on a plate; original Bep Viet image on transparency.
Khoảng 6 giờ 45 phút, gồm 2 giờ ngâm gạo: About 6 hours 45 minutes, including 2 hours of rice soaking and about 3 hours 40 minutes of drying; drying time varies with the weather.

Thời gian phơi thay đổi theo nắng và độ: Drying time changes with sun and humidity. Do not stack the crackers while they are still damp.
Nướng từng bánh trên than vừa, trở liên: Grill one cracker at a time over moderate charcoal, turning continuously so it crisps evenly without burning.
Chọn gạo thơm, hạt khô; vo sạch trước kh: Choose aromatic dry rice and rinse before soaking.
Sàng sạch; có thể rang sơ cho thơm trước: Sift clean; optionally toast lightly for extra aroma before steaming.

Chuẩn bị nồi tráng bánh có khăn căng sạc: Prepare a rice-steaming pot with a clean taut cloth and a flat drying surface. After steaming, separate each cracker and dry on a clean rack until just firm, usually about 3 hours 40 minutes depending on sun and humidity.
Khi nước trong nồi hấp sôi mạnh, múc một: When the water in the steamer is at a strong boil, ladle a very thin layer of batter onto the taut cloth, scatter a little sesame and cover for about 2–3 minutes until set. Spread a second thin layer over it and steam again until translucent and cooked through.
Nhấc bánh ra cẩn thận, dàn phẳng trên gi: Carefully lift off the cracker and lay it flat on a clean rack. Repeat with the remaining batter. Dry until pliable but no longer wet; do not let the crackers become brittle before grilling.
Nướng từng bánh trên than củi ở mức nhiệ: Grill each cracker over moderate charcoal, turning continuously until it puffs slightly, dries crisp and smells fragrant. Serve immediately.
Ram bắp Quảng Ngãi cuốn nhân bắp nếp non: Quang Ngai ram bap wraps young sticky corn with pork, shrimp, taro, shallot and chives in thin rice paper, then fries the rolls until golden. Bếp Việt edits a family-size recipe from local descriptions, keeping the sweet, tender corn filling and small crisp rolls.
Một đĩa khoảng 16 cuốn ram bắp nhỏ, dùng: About 16 small corn rolls, served as a shared side or starter for four.
Cuốn ram nhỏ vàng giòn, bên trong là nhâ: Small crisp golden rolls with a sweet, tender corn filling, fragrant chives and pepper, and a lightly savory taste from pork and shrimp.
Dọn nóng cùng rau sống, dưa leo và nước: Serve hot with fresh greens, cucumber and sweet-sour garlic fish sauce. The rolls can also be wrapped in rice paper with greens.

Bánh bó là bánh nếp ép thành đòn, gắn vớ: Bánh bó is a pressed glutinous-rice cake associated with Quang Ngai’s Lunar New Year spread. Toasted glutinous rice flour is bound with sugar syrup and mixed with candied coconut, pineapple, carrot, winter melon, tomato and ginger. Bếp Việt edits a small-batch home version using ready-made glutinous rice flour toasted at home.

Xu xoa Quảng Ngãi là thạch trong làm từ: Quang Ngai xu xoa is a clear jelly made from seaweed gathered along the local rocky shore. Dried seaweed is soaked and rinsed repeatedly, simmered with water and a little lemon until soft, then strained and left to set. Bếp Việt edits a small batch and serves it with fresh ginger sugar syrup, as locals do.
